chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A slave who is freed on the Day of 'Arafah.' He said: 'If one catches one of the two stations, then he has caught the Hajj.'

As for what he mentioned (may Allah have mercy on him) regarding the condition of being mature (baligh), it is necessary, because the obligation of Hajj applies only to one who is addressed by the conditions of taklif (legal responsibility). Among its conditions is the perfection of intellect ('aql). If the child is not perfect in intellect, Hajj is not obligatory upon him, and he only comes under the address (of the law) after the perfection of intellect. Therefore, what he does before that does not suffice him for what will be obligatory upon him in the future. And indicating this is also what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Hajj for a slave freed on the Day of 'Arafah and the conditions of maturity for its obligation?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that emancipation on the Day of 'Arafah immediately triggers the Hajj obligation, provided the individual has reached the age of maturity (bulugh) and perfection of intellect (kamal al-'aql), which are prerequisites for legal responsibility (taklif). This distinction ensures that while a child may perform Hajj, it serves as a voluntary act rather than fulfilling the future obligatory duty, a principle rooted in the general conditions of Mukallaf status.
